components.css: .ds-stage-nav { position: relative; } .ds-stage-list { position: relative; z-index: 1; display: flex; justify-content: space-between; margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; } .ds-stage-list li { width: 20%; } .ds-stage-progress { position: absolute; top: 14px; right: calc(20% - 7px); left: 7px; height: 1px; background: var(--line); } .ds-stage-progress::after { display: block; width: 50%; height: 1px; background: var(--ink); content: ""; transform-origin: left center; transition: width 300ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-stage { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: flex-start; gap: 6px; padding: 3px 0; border: 0; background: transparent; color: var(--soft); cursor: pointer; font: 570 14px/1.4 ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif; } .ds-stage:hover, .ds-stage[aria-current="step"] { color: var(--ink); } .ds-stage[aria-current="step"] { font-weight: 680; } .ds-stage.ds-stage--complete { color: var(--muted); } .ds-stage-dot { width: 14px; height: 14px; border: 1.5px solid #8b8b88; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--white); } .ds-stage[aria-current="step"] .ds-stage-dot, .ds-stage.ds-stage--complete .ds-stage-dot { border-color: var(--ink); background: var(--ink); } .ds-stage[aria-current="step"] .ds-stage-dot { box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px #e5e5e3; } .ds-stage:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 3px; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-stage-progress::after { transition-duration: 0.01ms; } }

narrative.overview:
BlindTender is a chain-of-custody instrument for one procurement event. A five-stage line keeps rules, bids, closure, award, and payment connected; a centered work area gives the current task room to read. The visual direction follows the user-pinned black-and-white discipline, clear large type, generous whitespace, rounded high-contrast controls, and short purposeful transitions. It takes the cited PamoSafe interface as a mood and layout reference without using its branding or content.

The interface stays flat and legible. Fine gray rules organize evidence rows and separate sections, while role and stage controls make the active state clear. Hashes, proofs, and trust notes remain in disclosure sections until a user asks to inspect them. Each screen focuses on its current task instead of presenting the complete operating model.

Motion marks a state change and then stops: controls respond quickly, the evidence line advances, and the active workspace enters once. Reduced-motion preferences remove the movement and smooth scrolling.
keyCharacteristics: One centered task area with evidence details progressively disclosed.
Quiet, finite motion with reduced-motion support.

rules.name: The Monochrome Rule
rules.body: Keep hierarchy and state in ink, neutral tints, line position, and text labels. Do not add a chromatic accent.

rules.name: The Task-First Type Rule
rules.body: Give the current task the largest type on the screen. Keep evidence labels clear and readable; do not shrink hashes or statuses to create density.

rules.name: The Flat Evidence Rule
rules.body: Use whitespace and fine rules to group evidence. Do not add card stacks, drop shadows, or decorative dashboard chrome.

dos: Do keep the page monochrome and reserve Working Ink for emphasis, selected states, and primary actions.
Do keep one primary task in view and reveal hashes, proofs, bid details, and trust notes through labeled disclosures.
Do keep the five-stage evidence thread visible and make its current stage clear to sighted and assistive-technology users.
Do wrap hashes and preserve their ability to be selected and copied.
Do keep transitions short and honor prefers-reduced-motion for animation, transitions, and scrolling.
donts: Don't introduce blue, green, red, or another accent hue into the interface.
Don't turn evidence into decorative terminal chrome, dense dashboard cards, or tiny labels.
Don't show every bid detail, hash, proof, and trust explanation in the default view.
Don't rely on color alone to communicate an outcome.
Don't use perpetual or attention-seeking animation.
